problem: Turn on the "YouTube Analytics API" in your Google Cloud project, then tap Analyze now again.
summary: Among the 12 films at least 2 days old, the best quarter had a median of 284.2 views per day, compared with 63.4 for the worst quarter. With three films in each group, the clearest early sign is that familiar objects paired with a visible, surprising result draw more views. The data cannot show what caused the gap or how many viewers stayed past the hook or reached the end.

working.lesson: Build the explanation around something viewers can see happen to a familiar object.
working.evidence: The top three show a spoon swinging into a stream of water (364.8 views/day), water lasting longer on a hotter pan (284.2), and raw and boiled eggs spinning differently (268.3).

working.lesson: State the surprising result in plain language when it makes viewers want to know why.
working.evidence: The hotter-pan film reached 284.2 views/day. Its opening is the only recorded first sentence in the top quarter, so this is an early sign from one film.

working.lesson: Give the demonstration enough time to show the result and explain it.
working.evidence: The top three ran 31, 34, and 38 seconds. The bottom three ran 25, 26, and 27 seconds. The 25-second brick-catching film also reached 258.2 views/day, so these results do not establish an ideal length.

notWorking.lesson: A surprising claim or a familiar setting alone gave mixed results.
notWorking.evidence: The tightrope film opens by saying a heavy pole makes a walker harder to topple and got 59.7 views/day. The Leonid meteor film got 63.4, and the above-freezing car-roof frost film got 113.6. Two of these three films have no recorded first…

notWorking.lesson: The two groups offer no basis for choosing a language, voice, media format, or hashtag strategy.
notWorking.evidence: Five of the six films are labeled en. The only en-US film is in the bottom quarter. All six have blank voice fields, are flagged as using real photos and no AI media, and carry eight hashtags including #science. The photo flag does not sho…

notWorking.lesson: The posting schedule has no clear winner yet.
notWorking.evidence: The top quarter posted Thursday at 09:00 and 14:00 and Friday at 09:00. The bottom quarter posted Tuesday at 10:00, Wednesday at 09:00, and Friday at 19:00. The 09:00 slot appears in both groups, and each day-and-hour combination appears o…

notWorking.lesson: Likes and comments cannot tell you where viewers stopped watching.
notWorking.evidence: The top three totaled 58 likes and 1 comment. The bottom three totaled 10 likes and 1 comment. No hook retention or end retention figures were supplied.

rules: Open on a familiar object already doing something surprising.
Name the object and the surprising result in the first sentence.
Put both outcomes in the same frame when a side-by-side comparison makes the difference clear.
Show the result before naming the physics principle.
Explain one cause and end when it answers the opening question.
moreTopics: Kitchen physics with a visible result
Side-by-side tests with familiar household objects
Everyday effects that reverse an intuitive prediction
hooks: Water lasts longer on a hotter pan.
experiments: Across comparable demonstrations, alternate a plain result statement with a short question. If retention becomes available, compare how many viewers stay past the opening sentence and reach the end.
Compare 25–28 seconds with 31–38 seconds across similar demonstrations. Use views per day measured at the same age for every film.
Rotate comparable films between 09:00 and 14:00 on the same weekday. Repeat each slot before comparing views per day at the same age.
